Kart physics from your data

Your limits this session: cornering 1.15 g, braking 0.61 g

Grip used: the g-g diagram

Grey dots: every moment of the session. Solid line: the edge of what you used (98th percentile). Dashed circles: 1.0 and 1.5 g; published cornering figures for 4-stroke rental karts fall in this range. The squashed bottom (braking 0.61 g against 1.15 g cornering) comes from rear-only brakes.

How hard the kart can accelerate

Each dot is a moment of acceleration; the line is the kart's limit at that speed (95th percentile, hills removed). It falls with speed, so exit speed carries down the straight.

Elevation along the lap

The track climbs about 2.7 m onto the bridge (around 230 m), then runs downhill into T3; the section under the bridge (around 420 m) sits lower. GPS height averaged over 14 laps.

How this was measured

  • Lap times are the official AMB times from your sheet. Everything else comes from the GoPro's GPS; GPS lap times match the sheet within 0.035 s on average (worst 0.14 s).
  • Track edges were traced from Esri satellite imagery by walking out from where the karts drove until the surface colour changes. 95% of edge points are confident. Edges more than 4 m beyond your widest line, or where connector roads join, are shown dashed as uncertain, because tyres that close those roads are not visible from above.
  • Drone photo (drone photo supplied by the driver): the photo was matched to your laps (rotation, scale, camera tilt), then corrected along the track so no lap runs through a tyre or grass and the tyre walls seen on video at T2, T4 land on the walls in the photo. From your widest line the edge walks outwards until 0.3 m of tyre or grass: 91% of edge points come from the photo (99% of them tyre walls), the rest from satellite imagery. Where both were sure, they agree within 1.1 m (median). Accuracy is about ±0.5–1 m; the bridge loop is hidden by trees, and tyres can move between the photo and your session.
  • Onboard video (GoPro HERO7 chin mount, GH011616/GH021616): at T2, T4 the satellite edge ran into connector asphalt, but the video shows a tyre wall right beside the kart. On laps where the kart passes the wall, the gap between the front wheel and the tyres was judged from the frame and added to that lap's GPS position plus half the kart width; the median sets the inside edge (about ±0.5 m). The video also shows traffic behind some flagged laps: lap 1 at T4, lap 10 at T4.
  • GPS drift: each lap's position was compared with the session average. The lap-to-lap spread was 0.70 m, so a smooth time-varying correction was applied. Lap points outside the edges went from 0.14% to 0.00%.
  • Noise floors measured from this session: line scatter on straights 0.40 m (upper bound), speed jitter 0.60 km/h. Differences smaller than twice these are not reported.
  • Braking: deceleration below 0.33 g held for at least 0.3 s, a threshold taken from the dip between lifting and braking in this session. Lighter slowing is labelled "light" (lift or light brake). The marker is where the main stop starts. No pedal sensors, so lifting and coasting are estimates.
  • Physics model: the smoothest line inside the edges (uncertain edges limited to 2 m beyond your line, 0.87 m kart margin), driven at your own grip and acceleration limits with perfect transitions. On your own best-lap path the same model gives 40.49 s against your 41.50 s, so treat its 38.34 s as an upper bound on what the kart could do, not a target.
  • Stitched target: one pass per section from that section's top 3, with speeds matching within 3.0 km/h at every join. The theoretical best (40.36 s) combines each section's single best and contains 5 impossible joins.
  • Statistics: Spearman correlation on clean passes, Benjamini–Hochberg correction across all 21 tests. Clean-lap filter: a corner minimum speed 5 km/h below your usual, or a section time above median + 3 × MAD.
